title: Gradient descent on a simple bowl

beats.text: How can we find the bottom of a curve? Start at x equals three on the bowl y equals x squared. Its height is nine.
The slope here is six. With a step size of one quarter, subtract one quarter times six. Our next position is one point five, and the height drops to two point two five.
Now the slope is three. Apply the same rule again: one point five minus one quarter times three gives zero point seven five. Each step follows the local slope downhill.

The update rule is x next equals x minus alpha times the derivative. On this simple bowl, our chosen step size moves us toward zero. Larger steps can overshoot, and general functions can have other local minima.
